answer: Depreciating identity bond stops bulk fakes by making idle identities costly: each identity posts a 100-credit bond, sealed with an opal stamp, losing 10 credits per epoch unless real work renews it. Renewal needs a steady stream of completed tasks; an identity that misses renewal is marked saffron and fades, so a dormant clone cannot copy one live agent. A zephyr of new clones still needs a fresh bond each, so keeping 1,000 fakes for ten epochs costs 100,000 credits in top-ups, with no bulk discount, while one honest agent renews its single bond from its earnings.
